behaviours.title: Balance of an account never seen is 0
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: it returns 0
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns undefined
contrary_alternatives: reading the balance of an unknown account throws an error
it returns null

behaviours.title: Entries of an account never seen is an empty list
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: it returns an empty list []
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns undefined
contrary_alternatives: reading entries of an unknown account throws an error

behaviours.title: Opening an existing account again keeps its balance and history
behaviours.given: account 'a' has received a deposit of 50 with txnId 'd1'
behaviours.then: balance('a') is still 50 and entries('a') still holds the one deposit entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the account is reset: balance('a') becomes 0 and entries('a') is empty
contrary_alternatives: opening an already-open account throws an 'account exists' error

behaviours.title: Opening a new account gives balance 0 and an empty history
behaviours.then: balance('a') is 0 and entries('a') is []
behaviours.contrary_then: the account starts with a non-zero balance such as 100
contrary_alternatives: the account's history starts with an 'opened' entry

behaviours.title: Deposit into an unopened account opens it and credits it
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'a' was never opened
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') is 100 and entries('a') is [{ txnId: 'd1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }]
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected and balance('a') stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with reason 'unknown-account'
the deposit is accepted but recorded with no history entry

behaviours.title: Deposit of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('a') stays 0 with no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit of 0 is accepted ({ ok: true }) and recorded as an entry of 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted silently with no entry recorded

behaviours.title: Deposit of a negative amount is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('a') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative deposit is accepted and the balance becomes 95
contrary_alternatives: the amount's sign is ignored and the balance becomes 105

behaviours.title: Deposit of NaN is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('a') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted ({ ok: true }) and the balance becomes NaN
contrary_alternatives: the deposit throws an error

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId reports success but credits only once
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') stays 100 and entries('a') still has one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is applied again: balance('a') becomes 200 with two entries
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A reused txnId on a different account or with a different amount is silently ignored
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } but balance('b') is 0 and balance('a') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit to 'b' is applied because it differs: balance('b') becomes 70
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and balance('b') stays 0

behaviours.title: Invalid amount is reported even when the txnId was already used
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } (amount checked before duplicate)
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns { ok: true } because the txnId was already processed
contrary_alternatives: it is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to 2 decimals (12.346 becomes 12.35)
behaviours.then: balance('a') is 12.35 and the entry amount is 12.35
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is kept unrounded: balance('a') is 12.346
contrary_alternatives: the amount is truncated to 12.34

behaviours.title: Rounding goes down below the half cent (12.344 becomes 12.34)
behaviours.then: balance('a') is 12.34
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is rounded up to 12.35
contrary_alternatives: the amount is kept as 12.344

behaviours.title: An exact half cent rounds up (0.125 becomes 0.13)
behaviours.then: balance('a') is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the half cent rounds to even/down and balance('a') is 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the amount is kept as 0.125

behaviours.title: A deposit below half a cent is accepted but rounds to a 0 entry
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') is 0 and entries('a') holds an entry { txnId: 'd1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 0 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected with reason 'invalid-amount' because it rounds to 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted with balance 0.004
the deposit is accepted but no entry is recorded

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') is 0 and the last entry is { txnId: 'w1', kind: 'withdrawal', amount: 100 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'insufficient-funds' and the balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected because a minimum balance must remain

behaviours.title: Withdrawing one cent more than the balance is rejected
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('a') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes -0.01
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is capped and the balance becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawal amount is rounded before checking funds (10.004 from 10 succeeds)
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and balance('a') is 0 (amount rounded to 10)
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with 'insufficient-funds' because 10.004 exceeds 10
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through and the balance becomes -0.004

behaviours.title: Withdrawing from an account never opened is rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('a') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: it is rejected with reason 'unknown-account'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal goes through and balance becomes -1

behaviours.title: Withdrawal of 0 or a negative amount is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('a') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the -20 withdrawal is accepted and the balance becomes 120
contrary_alternatives: the 0 withdrawal is accepted as a no-op returning { ok: true }

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal with the same txnId reports success but debits once
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 100 and withdraw('a', 30, 'w1') has succeeded
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and balance('a') stays 70
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is applied again and the balance becomes 40
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and balance stays 70

behaviours.title: txnIds are shared across operation types: a withdrawal reusing a deposit's txnId is ignored
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } but balance('a') stays 100 and no withdrawal entry is added
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is applied since it is a different kind of operation: balance becomes 60
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not use up its txnId
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 50 and withdraw('a', 80, 'w1') was rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.when: deposit('a', 50, 'd2') is made and withdraw('a', 80, 'w1') is retried
behaviours.then: the retry returns { ok: true } and balance('a') is 20
behaviours.contrary_then: the retry is treated as a duplicate: returns { ok: true } but balance stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the retry is rejected with reason 'duplicate' and balance stays 100

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of exactly 5000 is within the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 6000 and nothing has been withdrawn
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and balance('a') is 1000
behaviours.contrary_then: it is rejected with 'daily-limit' and balance stays 6000
contrary_alternatives: the limit is 1000 and the withdrawal is rejected

behaviours.title: A single withdrawal of 5000.01 exceeds the daily limit
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 6000 and nothing has been withdrawn
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('a') stays 6000
behaviours.contrary_then: it is accepted and balance('a') becomes 999.99
contrary_alternatives: 5000 is paid out and the remaining 0.01 is refused

behaviours.title: The daily limit is cumulative across withdrawals: 3000 + 2000 is allowed, a further 0.01 is not
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 10000 and has withdrawn 3000 ('w1') and 2000 ('w2') successfully
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('a') stays 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit applies only per withdrawal, so it is accepted and balance becomes 4999.99
contrary_alternatives: the second withdrawal of 2000 would already have been refused

behaviours.title: Funds are checked before the daily limit
behaviours.when: withdraw('a', 6000, 'w1') is called (over both balance and daily limit)
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' }
contrary_alternatives: it is accepted and the balance becomes -5900

behaviours.title: Daily limit is tracked per account
behaviours.given: accounts 'a' and 'b' each hold 6000 and 'a' has withdrawn 5000
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and balance('b') is 1000
behaviours.contrary_then: it is rejected with 'daily-limit' because the limit is shared across accounts

behaviours.title: Withdrawal rounding applies to the daily limit (5000.004 counts as 5000)
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and balance('a') is 1000
behaviours.contrary_then: it is rejected with 'daily-limit' because 5000.004 exceeds 5000

behaviours.title: A withdrawal refused for daily-limit does not count toward the limit
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 10000 and withdraw('a', 4000, 'w1') succeeded, then withdraw('a', 1500, 'w2') was refused for daily-limit
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true } and balance('a') is 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the refused 1500 still counted, so it is rejected with 'daily-limit'

behaviours.title: Transfer moves money and records an entry on each side
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') is 60, balance('b') is 40, 'a' gets { txnId: 't1', kind: 'transfer-out', amount: 40 } and 'b' gets { txnId: 't1', kind: 'transfer-in', amount: 40 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected because 'b' was never opened, and balances stay 100 and 0
contrary_alternatives: only the sending account records an entry

behaviours.title: Transferring exactly the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') is 0 and balance('b') is 100
behaviours.contrary_then: it is rejected with 'insufficient-funds' and balances stay 100 and 0

behaviours.title: Transferring one cent more than the balance is rejected, both balances unchanged
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, balance('a') stays 100, balance('b') stays 0 and 'b' has no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: it is accepted, 'a' becomes -0.01 and 'b' becomes 100.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is moved

behaviours.title: Transfer of 0 or a negative amount is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: both return { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balances stay 100 and 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the -10 transfer is accepted and moves money backwards: 'a' becomes 110 and 'b' -10
contrary_alternatives: the 0 transfer is accepted as a no-op

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId reports success but moves money once
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') stays 60 and balance('b') stays 40
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied again: 'a' becomes 20 and 'b' becomes 80
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is rejected with reason 'duplicate'

behaviours.title: Transfers do not count toward the daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.given: account 'a' holds 10000 and has withdrawn 5000 today
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') is 2000 and balance('b') is 3000
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected with 'daily-limit' and balance('a') stays 5000

behaviours.title: Transfer to the same account leaves the balance unchanged but records two entries
behaviours.then: it returns { ok: true }, balance('a') stays 100 and entries('a') gains a transfer-out of 30 then a transfer-in of 30
behaviours.contrary_then: the self-transfer is rejected and no entries are added
contrary_alternatives: the balance is debited without being credited and becomes 70

behaviours.title: Transfer amounts are rounded to 2 decimals
behaviours.then: balance('b') is 10.01 and the transfer-in entry amount is 10.01
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is kept unrounded: balance('b') is 10.006
contrary_alternatives: the amount is truncated to 10

behaviours.title: entries returns a copy; changing it does not change the ledger
behaviours.when: the list returned by entries('a') has an item pushed onto it
behaviours.then: entries('a') read again still has length 1
behaviours.contrary_then: entries('a') now has length 2
